lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
integration_oidc-adminSettings.js: 1 file, 3,174,230 B, and 4 chunks of 176,170 B its runtime loads later, of which integration_oidc-adminSettings.js is 3,174,230 B (94.7 %).
integration_oidc-personalSettings.js: 1 file, 3,159,493 B, and 4 chunks of 176,170 B its runtime loads later, of which integration_oidc-personalSettings.js is 3,159,493 B (94.7 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,455,130 B in 216 modules, 45.8 % of the static path of integration_oidc-adminSettings.js, imported by its root in components/AdminSettings.vue (NcActionButton, NcActions, NcButton, ...) and components/PersonalSettings.vue (NcActionButton, NcActions, NcButton, ...).
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

62 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 142,657 B, 4.5 % of the static path of integration_oidc-adminSettings.js, next to 6 components the source names and 9 those pull in.
NcRichText 45,331 B, NcCheckboxRadioSwitch 12,549 B, NcDateTimePicker 8,589 B, NcAppSidebar 7,350 B, NcRelatedResourcesPanel 6,827 B, NcModal 6,824 B, and 56 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

6 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
